title: The Elder Scrolls
wiki_lead:
The Elder Scrolls is a series of action role-playing video games primarily developed by Bethesda Game Studios and published by Bethesda Softworks. The series focuses on free-form gameplay in an open world. Most games in the series have been critically and commercially successful, with The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind (2002), The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion (2006) and The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (2011) all winning Game of the Year awards from multiple outlets. The series has sold more than 90 million copies worldwide.
Within the series' fictional universe, each game takes place on the continent of Tamriel. The setting combines pre-medieval real-world elements, such as a powerful Roman-like Empire, with high fantasy medieval themes, including limited technology, widespread magic use, and the existence of many mythological creatures. The continent is split into a number of provinces inhabited by humans and humanoid fantasy races such as elves, orcs and anthropomorphic animals. A common theme in the lore is that a chosen hero (represented by the player's character) rises to defeat an impending threat, typically a malevolent being or an antagonistic army.
Since debuting with The Elder Scrolls: Arena in 1994, the series has produced a total of five main games (of which the last three have each featured two or three expansions) as well as several spin-offs. In 2014, a massively multiplayer online role-playing game, The Elder Scrolls Online, was released by Bethesda's affiliated ZeniMax subsidiary ZeniMax Online Studios.

Development history


Before The Elder Scrolls

Prior to working on The Elder Scrolls series, Bethesda had worked predominantly with sports and action games. In the six years from its founding to Arena's 1994 release, Bethesda had released ten games, six of them sports games, with titles such as Hockey League Simulator, NCAA Basketball: Road to the Final Four ('91/'92 Edition), and Wayne Gretzky Hockey, and the remaining four adaptations from other media, primarily the Terminator series. Bethesda's course changed abruptly when it began working on its first action role-playing game. Designer Ted Peterson recalls: "I remember talking to the guys at Sir-Tech who were doing Wizardry VII: Crusaders of the Dark Savant at the time, and them literally laughing at us for thinking we could do it." Ted Peterson worked alongside Vijay Lakshman as one of the initial designers of what became known as Arena, a "medieval-style gladiator game".


Arena

Peterson and Lakshman were joined by Julian LeFay who, according to Peterson, "really spear-headed the initial development of the series". Peterson, Lakshman, and LeFay were longtime aficionados of pen-and-paper role-playing games, which greatly influenced the creation of the world of Tamriel. grok_lead: The Elder Scrolls is an action role-playing video game franchise developed and published primarily by Bethesda Softworks, known for its immersive open-world environments set in the fictional continent of Tamriel. The series emphasizes player freedom, deep narrative choices, and expansive lore spanning multiple eras of history, with gameplay focusing on exploration, questing, and character progression in a high-fantasy setting populated by diverse races, gods, and mythical creatures. Since its inception, The Elder Scrolls has sold over 90 million copies across its mainline titles and spin-offs as of 2023, establishing it as one of the most influential RPG series in gaming history. The franchise originated in 1994 with The Elder Scrolls: Arena, a dungeon-crawling RPG initially conceived as a gladiatorial combat simulator but expanded into a full exploration of Tamriel to rescue Emperor Uriel Septim VII from a curse. This was followed by The Elder Scrolls Chapter II: Daggerfall in 1996, which introduced a massive procedurally generated world twice the size of Great Britain, intricate political intrigue, and guild systems, though it was limited by the technology of the era. The series gained widespread acclaim with The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind in 2002, praised for its alien-like island of Vvardenfell, non-linear storytelling, and innovative skill-based progression that allowed players to shape their hero through actions rather than classes. Subsequent mainline entries built on this foundation: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion (2006) featured a radiant AI system for dynamic NPC behaviors and the province of Cyrodiil during a demonic invasion, while The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (2011) shifted to the frozen north amid a dragon apocalypse and civil war, becoming a cultural phenomenon with over 60 million copies sold as of 2023 and extensive modding support. Spin-offs have expanded the universe, including the massively multiplayer online role-playing game The Elder Scrolls Online (2014), which explores the Second Era's Three Banners War across all of Tamriel, and mobile titles like The Elder Scrolls: Blades (2020), focusing on dungeon crawling and castle building. A sixth mainline installment, The Elder Scrolls VI, was announced in 2018 but remains in development as of 2025, with no confirmed release date. At its core, The Elder Scrolls unfolds across a rich timeline divided into erasâthe Merethic (prehistoric migrations and the Dragon War), First (rise of empires and the disappearance of the Dwemer), Second (interregnum and Tiber Septim's conquests), Third (Septim dynasty and the Oblivion Crisis), and Fourth (post-empire turmoil including the Great War and Alduin's return)âwoven with themes of prophecy, divinity, and mortal ambition. The lore draws from influences like Norse mythology and Tolkien-esque fantasy, featuring ten playable races such as Nords, Elves, and Argonians, alongside pantheons of gods like the Eight Divines and Daedric Princes who intervene in mortal affairs. This depth encourages replayability, as player decisions can alter outcomes, join factions, or even become legendary figures like the Nerevarine or Dragonborn. The series' hallmark is its sandbox-style gameplay, where nonlinear quests, skill trees, and environmental interactions foster emergent storytelling, supported by robust modding communities that extend longevity through custom content. Critically, it has earned numerous awards, including Game of the Year for Morrowind, Oblivion, and Skyrim, and has influenced modern open-world design in titles like The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077. Beyond games, the franchise extends to novels, comics, and tabletop adaptations, cementing its status as a cornerstone of fantasy gaming.
